title: {Les Fêtes}
description: French holidays and celebrations - from Bastille Day to crêpe day!

vocabulary.note: April 1 - stick paper fish on backs!

sections.heading: {Les Jours Fériés} (National Holidays)
sections.text: France has 11 official public holidays - more than most countries!
sections.example: {le Nouvel An} (Jan 1), {Pâques} (Easter), {la Fête Nationale} (July 14 - Bastille Day), {Noël} (Dec 25)

sections.heading: Bastille Day - {La Fête Nationale}
sections.text: July 14 - France's most important holiday celebrating the French Revolution (1789)
sections.example: {Military parade on Champs-Élysées, fireworks, parties} - like July 4th in America but with more cheese!

sections.heading: Religious Holidays
sections.text: France is secular but many Catholic holidays are still official days off
sections.example: {Pâques} (Easter), Ascension, Pentecôte (Pentecost), Assomption (Aug 15), Toussaint (Nov 1 - All Saints)

sections.heading: WWI & WWII Commemorations
sections.text: France honors both world wars with official holidays

sections.heading: Fun French Traditions
sections.text: Unique celebrations you won't find everywhere!
sections.example: {la Chandeleur} (Feb 2 - Crêpe Day!), {le Poisson d'Avril} (April 1 - stick fish on backs!), {la Fête de la Musique} (June 21 - free concerts everywhere!)

sections.heading: Christmas & New Year ({Les Réveillons})
sections.text: Two huge celebrations with fancy dinners called '{réveillons}'
sections.example: {le Réveillon de Noël} (Christmas Eve dinner), {le Réveillon du Nouvel An} (New Year's Eve), {la Galette des Rois} (Jan 6 - King Cake with hidden prize!)

sections.heading: Quebec Holidays
sections.example: {la Saint-Jean-Baptiste} (June 24 - Quebec National Day), {le Jour du Souvenir} (Nov 11 - Remembrance Day)

sections.heading: Holiday Greetings
sections.example: {Joyeux Noël!} (Merry Christmas!), {Bonne année!} (Happy New Year!), {Joyeuses Pâques!} (Happy Easter!), {Bon anniversaire!} (Happy Birthday!)
